findings.text: follow-on: the added clause asserts of the code subject that 'the guard cannot pass a report whose own grammar reads nothing in it', and that is measurably false. report_carries_review_lines matches the *plan* patterns on the lines the health reader yields, but parse_health_review keeps a RUBRIC line only when the item it names is in HEALTH_REVIEW_ITEMS (review.py:1485) and a FINDING only under _HEALTH_FINDING_LINE_RE with the same membership test. HEALTH_REVIEW_ITEMS and PLAN_REVIEW_ITEMS are disjoint, so a code report whose only emitted line reads 'RUBRIC evidence: pass' plus a TREATMENT line passes the guard (report_carries_review_lines -> True) while parse_health_review returns rubric_items {} and findings [] and all six items absent: the guard admits a code report its own grammar reads nothing in, and _code_review_record stores it with every rubric item absent — the composed-but-undelivered false pass the guard exists to prevent. Measured at the reviewed head with plan_review.report_carries_review_lines(rep, subject='code') and review.parse_health_review(rep): guard=True, items={}, findings=[], absent=6 for 'RUBRIC bogus: pass' and for 'RUBRIC evidence: pass'. This is pre-existing rather than introduced — the base guard at d85e543c read every subject through _review_text_lines with the same plan patterns, so the repair restores base behaviour exactly — but the claim is new in this diff and a reader would rely on it, so it is recorded rather than scored as a regression.

follow-on: _report_line_reader re-tests the subject that delivered_report_record already branches on at plan_review.py:2154, so the subject->dialect mapping now lives in two independent places, and its default (subject='' or any subject other than 'code') is the permissive plan reading. A caller that reads a code report without passing subject='code' therefore re-opens exactly the guard/parser divergence the repair closes, and no case delivers a code report through the default subject — the two added tests both pass subject='code' or reach it through delivered_report_record. Preferring one dispatch would remove the second place for the mapping to drift.

follow-on: 'sorted(record["rubric_items"]) == sorted(CODE_ITEMS)' compares the stored record against the same constant _code_report used to build the report text the test handed in, so the two sides derive from one source and the assertion cannot tell a correct parse from a code path that echoes back the items it was given. It does redden when the record drops items, so it is coverage; it would be independent with a hand-written expected item list.
